title: Caldou with Lemon
author: Amina Savoura
desc: Small fish blanched, never fried, in lightly browned onions and a litre of salted water, finished with the juice of four lemons and served with rice.
longDesc: The Afrik caldou is one sentence of introduction — ‘a recipe from the Casamance’ — and a short method. A kilo of rice cooks gently in two litres of salted water. A very large onion, sliced, softens in hot groundnut oil; the small fish are added and ‘blanchis, mais pas frits’, then salted, peppered and covered with a litre of salted water. They simmer for a quarter of an hour, the lemon juice goes in, and cooking continues a few minutes more before everything is served with the rice.
ingredients: 3 or 4 spoonfuls of peanut oil — spoon size not specified
Salt and pepper — quantities not printed
2 litres salted water for the rice, plus 1 litre salted water for the fish
steps: Bring 2 litres of salted water to a boil in a pot and add the washed rice. Cook over low heat.
Slice the onion and soften it in hot peanut oil.
Lay the fish in the pot and blanch them — do not fry. Salt, pepper, then pour in 1 litre of salted water.
Let simmer a quarter of an hour.
Continue cooking a few minutes and serve with the rice.
chefTips: ‘Blanchir, mais pas frire’ is the one cue the source gives — the fish should turn pale in the pan, not take colour.
A quarter of an hour at a bare simmer — the printed time — is the whole cooking of the fish.
Add the lemon juice after the simmer, not before: acid early toughens the fish.
The source gives no browning target for the onion, only ‘hot oil’.
commonMistakes: Frying the fish in the oil.
healthBenefits: Whole small fish supply calcium (if the bones are eaten), protein and omega-3.
culturalNote: Afrik’s one-line introduction places caldou in the Casamance. A third printing, ‘Caldou ou Kaldou au Bissap’ (with hibiscus), is named on the same site and was not read.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Caldou ou Kaldou au citron’. Byline exactly as printed: ‘Amina Savoura’. Publication: Afrik. Date as printed: ‘Publié le 13 avril 2012 à 15h46’. Yield: ‘Pour 8 personnes’. Times as printed: preparation 1 heure, cooking 1 heure. Introduction in full: ‘Une recette de Casamance.’ TWO-PASS; the second pass flagged the same printed error independently.
PRINTED ERROR kept: ‘déposez les poisson’ (missing plural), confirmed as printed on both passes.

Cues in short fragments: ‘faites blanchir, mais pas frire’; ‘Laissez frémir un quart d’heure’. ABSENT, not estimated: any colour cue for the onion, the duration of the rice, and the ‘quelques minutes’ after the lemon.

UNRECONCILED with SEN032: Harris browns the onions ‘until soft and golden brown, about 16 minutes’ before liquid; Savoura simply softens them. Harris uses two 1 1/2-lb whole snappers and 4 cups of water; Savoura 1 kg of small fish and 1 litre. Harris splits 1/2 cup of lemon juice into two additions; Savoura adds the juice of four lemons once. Neither averaged.
A line in a Fine Dining Lovers overview (Mathilde Bourge, 2018) defines caldou as fish ‘cooked in palm oil’; both full recipes use peanut oil. Recorded, not resolved.
